html:
The Nahua are the peoples of central Mexico who speak Nahuatl, the language of the Aztecs. They are the largest Indigenous group of Mexico; today over a million people speak Nahuatl.

Nahuatl speakers spread into central Mexico from the north, probably in the centuries after 500. The Toltecs of Tula were likely Nahua, and so were the Mexica who founded Tenochtitlan in 1325 and built the Triple Alliance with Texcoco and Tlacopan. Nahuatl became the common language of Mesoamerica, and many words, such as tomato, chocolate and avocado, came into English through it.

After the Spanish conquest, Nahuatl was written in the Latin alphabet, and a large body of colonial writing survives. The map places this label just west of the Valley of Mexico. See also Nahuas and the Mexica.
